newsitem.title: USA: Prime minister says Portugal certain to join euro.
newsitem.headline: Prime minister says Portugal certain to join euro.

text.p: Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres said on Saturday he had no doubt Portugal would become a founder member of the single European currency and that the country's ambitious privatization program was on track.

Guterres told Reuters in San Francisco that he was "100 percent sure" Portugal would be amongst the European elite to launch the single currency in 1999 because the country would meet the economic requirements for entry.
"I am determined," Guterres said in the interview, adding that recent economic developments in Portugal were "extremely encouraging."
European Union countries are racing to cut deficits and public debt to levels demanded by the Maastricht treaty in order to qualify for economic and monetary union.

Guterres said Portugal's privatization program has been a "total success" thus far, and that he has had meetings with potential investors in the United States about upcoming deals involving Portuguese utility EDP-Electricidade de Portugal and other state companies.
"What I'm trying to do is create the proper environment for them (the privatizations) to be successful," he said.

The partial privatization of EDP should take place in May, but certainly "before the summer," Guterres said, adding that the first tranche would represent 25 percent of EDP. That deal would be followed by other tranches, Guterres said.

Guterres said he would like to privatize Portuguese state airline TAP-Air Portugal as soon as possible. "We hope for an early privatization (of TAP), as early as possible. If possible, next year," he said.

But Guterres said TAP's privatization would depend on its ability to find strategic partners. The Socialist government of Guterres has said TAP must conclude its restructuring plan before forming any strategic alliances with foreign airlines.

Guterres reiterated his country's determination to join the euro. Asked if he had any doubts Portugal would join Europe's common currency from the start in 1999, he said: "I cannot imagine being anything less than 100 percent sure."
The Maastricht treaty lays down specific economic targets on inflation, interest and exchange rates, budget deficits and public debt which nations must meet in order to join the euro from the start.
Guterres said Portugal would pass the entry tests. He cited the country's declining debt ratios and budget deficit, and said, "there is no problem with inflation any more."
Reiterating comments he made earlier this week in Washington, Guterres said he strongly supported NATO expansion. He also said Saturday that Russia has no reason to "fear" NATO enlargement.
"What I think we need is a substantial dialogue between NATO and Russia," he told Reuters. "What I would like in the foreseeable future would be a real alliance between NATO and Russia."

NATO leaders are to meet in Madrid in July to decide which will be the first nations invited to join an enlarged alliance. Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are expected to be among the first new members.
Before leaving California, Guterres said he would visit Silicon Valley for the first time to promote Portugal as "a location for high technology investment."
